Hannah / Monica — quick note from the audit side: auditors generally treat the assessment period as inclusive of the listed end-date. Point-in-time tests are performed as of the last day of the period (often a single point such as 2025-12-31), and any change after that day would typically be outside scope unless explicitly covered by a bridge letter or subsequent attestation.

In practice we say: "The examination covered the period from 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (inclusive)." That language makes the inclusive nature explicit. I can check with our audit firm contact if you'd like verbatim wording from their report.

On the bridge letter: we routinely provide a short management representation that there were no material changes to controls since the report cutoff, dated as of the signing date. That letter should be drafted by us, reviewed by Legal, and then signed by an authorized officer. Monica, happy to loop in Legal if you want me to coordinate.

Rishi
Senior Manager, Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference
